findings.summary: Spec §2.2 recovery type 5 (orphan .git/index.lock whose holder PID is dead) is inert in reality. orphan_index_lock_path() decides ownership by parsing the lock file's text as an integer PID, but Git's lockfile API never writes a PID into .git/index.lock — the file holds the serialized new index (binary, starting with 'DIRC') or is empty when the holder died before writing. Both cases fall into the ValueError/empty branch, yield holder_pid = 0, and return None, so a genuine orphan lock is never removed. The only coverage (mcp/kernel/tests/test_reconcile.py:172-182 and mcp/kernel/tests/test_atomicity.py:158-176) fabricates '999999\n' as the lock content, which no Git version produces, so the frozen acceptance in spec §4.3 and Article V test-reality parity are satisfied only against a synthetic artifact.

wf_reconcile does not meet the governance/idempotency contract frozen in spec §2.2 and §5.3 ('受 MCP 治理、幂等（同 idempotency_key 幂等）、B 类'). The tool takes only scope_prefixes/control_paths, has no idempotency_key parameter, does not route through _server_mutation, and never records a claim in the mutation ledger — unlike every other mutating wf_/fs_ tool in the same file (wf_create:481, wf_save:506, wf_resume:533, wf_append_progress:550, wf_reindex:571, fs_create:659, …). Repeating the same call therefore re-executes tree-mutating recovery (quarantine moves, git reset, resume commits) with no idempotent replay.

_quarantine_untracked derives the destination deterministically from the source path (sha256(path)[:12] / basename), so quarantining the same repo-relative path twice makes shutil.move overwrite the previously quarantined copy. On the same filesystem shutil.move degrades to os.rename, which replaces the existing destination silently, so a second wf_reconcile over a recreated path destroys the first rescued file. This defeats the 'move to runtime root and leave a pointer' guarantee of spec §2.2 type 1 and makes the recovery lossy rather than reversible.

Recovery type 1 quarantines every untracked, non-ignored file unconditionally. Spec §2.2 type 1 requires an EK-4 artifact-class judgment ('产物类别（EK-4 判据）移送 runtime root 留指针，否则 commit 或确认后丢弃'), but only the move branch is implemented and no classification exists. Worse, _under_scope returns True for all paths when scope_prefixes is empty (kernel.py:276-283), and wf_reconcile defaults scope_prefixes to None, so the default tool call relocates every uncommitted user file in the whole volume into .katana/runtime/recovered/. mcp/work-folder/tests/test_reconcile.py:79-93 asserts exactly this behavior on an ordinary user file.

The quarantine destination is only registered as an allowed ignored runtime path for git_tracked=False bindings; _runtime_state_allowances returns [] immediately for git_tracked=True. memory and wiki bind TransactionManifest with the default git_tracked=True (mcp/memory/katana_memory_mcp/server.py:127,320 and mcp/wiki/katana_wiki_mcp/server.py:73), so for those bindings the type-1 move lands in <root>/.katana/recovered, which is neither ignored nor allowed. reconcile(recover=True) would move the file and then still fail the clean gate with BROKEN, permanently displacing content without recovering anything. Spec §2.2 requires the kernel reconcile logic to be one implementation reused by all three services.

_recover_governed_state accepts control_paths but never references it in the body. require_clean_working_tree blocks on dirt inside scopes + control_paths (gitops.py:513-525), so under a scoped reconcile any untracked dirt on a governance control surface is unrecoverable and always ends in BROKEN, while the parameter's presence implies otherwise. The dead parameter is either a lost exemption or a lost recovery branch; either way the intent is not expressed in code.

Spec §2.2 type 6 requires the structured BROKEN diagnosis to carry mutation_id/paths/suggested commands. _unrecoverable_scene_error declares a mutation_id keyword but no call site ever supplies it — reconcile's only invocation (kernel.py:242) passes just the binding — so the reconcile BROKEN envelope always reports "mutation_id": null, and mcp/work-folder/katana_work_folder_mcp/server.py:419 surfaces that null to the operator. The residue can never be attributed to a mutation.

_recover_governed_state runs before the clean gate, so in a mixed scene (recoverable types 1/3/5 plus an unattributable tracked modification) files are already moved, unstaged, or committed by the time require_clean_working_tree raises and the call returns BROKEN. That contradicts the spec §2.2 guarantee that the type-6 outcome 不动树, and the returned diagnosis does not report the mutations already applied, so the operator's manual recovery starts from a scene that silently differs from the one they observed.

_sync_real_index_isolated copies .git/index, edits the copy under a temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE, and os.replace()s it back without ever taking .git/index.lock. This removes the contention the spec targeted, but it is a read-modify-write with no mutual exclusion against non-governed Git processes: a concurrent plain `git add` that legitimately holds index.lock has its result silently clobbered by the replace. Governed transactions are serialized by repository_mutation_lock (gitops.py:323-351), so the exposure is bounded to external Git use, but the spec §2.1 invariant '同步语义不变（事务条目 + 非 allowlist 的 staged 条目保留不动）' is no longer guaranteed under concurrency.

The quarantine audit pointer is best-effort: the manifest append is wrapped in `except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError): pass`, so the file is moved even when the pointer record fails to persist, leaving an unattributable relocation. The same block also calls existing.append() on whatever json.loads returns, so a quarantine-manifest.json that is a JSON object rather than a list raises an uncaught AttributeError after the move has already happened.
